title: What If a Sound Got Louder Than 194 Decibels? Air Says No

scenes.text: What if a sound got louder than 194 decibels? In Earth's air, it simply stops being sound.
Sound is air pressure swinging above and below normal. Normal is one atmosphere.
The low side can only drop to a vacuum, zero pressure. It cannot go lower.
So the biggest possible swing is two atmospheres. That works out to about 194 decibels.
Push harder and the wave becomes a shock wave, a sudden wall of pressure.
Krakatoa in 1883 came close. About 160 kilometers away, its pressure spike hit roughly 172 decibels.

description:
What if a sound got louder than 194 decibels?
In Earth's air, 194 decibels is the limit before a wave becomes a shock wave.
